title: Rav Hamnuna (IV)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was like a colleague of Rava and Abaye, as in Nazir 64b: “Rav Hamnuna said: A nazirite … Rava objected … he said to him: I concede to you … Rava said to him: I too concede to you … Abaye said to him: But,” etc. In Temurah 25b: “Rava challenges it … Rav Hamnuna said to him: Rabbi Elazar is Rabbi Yochanan’s student — and you say Rabbi Yochanan’s reason?” etc. In Makkot 2b: “Rav Hamnuna thought to say … Rava said to him,” etc. In Yevamot 41a: “Rava said: What is Rav’s reason? … Rav Hamnuna objected … (Rava) was silent; after he left he said: Why did you not say to him,” etc. In Shabbat 10a Rava saw Rav Hamnuna prolonging his prayer and said: “They leave eternal life and occupy themselves with temporary life.”

Hyman concludes clearly from all these places that this is not the Rav Hamnuna who was the colleague of Rabbah and Rav Yosef, but a later Rav Hamnuna. This Rav Hamnuna is mentioned in Niddah 27a: “Rav Papa sat behind Rav Bivi before Rav Hamnuna.” Hyman suggests that this Rav Hamnuna is the one who disagrees with Rav Chanan of Nehardea, as in Shabbat 82a; and Rav Huna bar Sechorah was standing before Rav Hamnuna and fed him a piece of meat; Rav Huna said to him, “Were it not that you are Rav Hamnuna, I would not feed you”: Chullin 107a.

In Berakhot 60a: “Yehudah bar Natan was walking after Rav Hamnuna; he sighed. He said to him: Does that man want suffering?” Hyman prefers the Dikdukei Soferim reading Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Natan, the son of Rabbi Natan the Tanna; it reads there: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Natan was walking after Rabbi in the market of Tiberias; he saw him,” etc.

The various Hamnuna separations and Berakhot textual proposal remain Hyman’s.
